scope: Only the two previously outstanding requested local regression scenarios; this does not assert CI readiness.
diagnosis: Current code and tests already contain the selected fixes. The outstanding failure was missing native execution evidence, not a product defect requiring new edits. The old installer was rejected by the current checksum regression as expected.

scenarios.name: Run the focused regression without GNU sha256sum: the real shasum backend passes.
scenarios.live_interface: Native execution of tests/fm-remote-hands.test.sh and the current production prepare executable; real /usr/bin/core_perl/shasum computes the digest and checks the checksum stream.
scenarios.observed: Exit 0; initial test PATH lacks sha256sum; actual backend invocation records show -a 256 for digest computation and -a 256 -c - for verification from the private download directory.

scenarios.name: Run regressions after login PATH reordering and against the old installer: fixtures remain private, preserve the archive sentinel, and clean up after assertion failure.
scenarios.live_interface: Real Bash -lc initialization reads the namespace-local /etc/profile and prepends system paths; the current regression executes unchanged current and pre-fix production preparation scripts.
scenarios.observed: Current installer exit 0; old installer exit 1 with missing checksum must fail prepare. Actual copy records stay under fixture-tmp, SHA records verify from the private download directory, sentinel hashes remain identical, and fixture-tmp is empty after both success and assertion failure.
